title: Slot compaction regression causing intermittent batch deserts — runbook & mitigations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-01 and intermittently thereafter, a scheduler regression introduced in runtime-1.24 caused the slot compaction routine to collapse active slot metadata incorrectly. This resulted in windows that appeared empty to the coalescer while requests were queued, producing multi-second 'batch deserts' (periods where no batches were formed). Symptoms included tail latency spikes, unfair request starvation across priorities, and elevated 5xx retries from upstream clients. This ticket captures the investigative notes, immediate mitigations, a permanent fix plan, and runbook updates.

investigation_summary: Observables: coalescer logs showed repeated 'empty-window' markers while request queues had non-zero length; RPC traces demonstrated queuing without dispatch. Metric correlations: batch_count per-second dropped by 60% during deserts while inflight requests increased; KV cache eviction rate rose by 2x before deserts. Root instrumentation: instrumented compaction routine and added sequence numbers; capturing a race where the compactor advanced the slot epoch and GC'd a live slot because its 'last_touch' timestamp was from a preempted worker. Reproduction: synthetic load with mixed short and long-context requests reproduced the condition in a local replica with high concurrency (>= 400 qps).
root_cause: A regression in the slot compaction subsystem (merged during runtime-1.24) changed the ordering between epoch advancement and in-flight slot pinning. Under bursty traffic with interleaved long-context requests, compaction could remove a slot that was still logically active for a different worker. This introduced a state where the scheduler considered the window empty even though requests were waiting, causing the coalescer to skip formation. Secondary contributor: a missing invariant check between the slot pin API and compactor that would have prevented GC of pinned slots.
mitigations_applied:
1) Immediate feature-flag rollback: disabled aggressive compaction on all hosts (rolled out in 18 minutes).
2) Watchdog: added a short-lived guard that prevents compaction if queue depth > threshold.
3) Canary rollback verification: validated that batch formation returned to baseline on canaries before full roll out.
4) Customer-facing mitigation: rate-limiting adjustments and temporary autoscale bump for affected customers with tight SLOs.

rollout_plan: Patch will land on a branch and be validated by CI and the new deterministic test. We will run a 48-hour canary in us-west-2 (10% of fleet) with traffic shaping to mimic peak patterns. If no regressions are observed, perform a staged rollout by region at 25% intervals with 30-minute observation windows and automated rollback on SLO regressions. Target merge date: 2026-03-18; full fleet rollout by 2026-03-22 if canary passes.
